subject: DPA countersign pathways and DocuSign routing for Globex
body:
From: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@globex.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@globex.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood DPA redlines + execution logistics

Tessa —

Thanks for sending the revised DPA. Our legal team reviewed the PDF and sent back a small set of follow-ups (attached). Before we re-redline in DocuSign we want to confirm: who at Redwood should be the initial signer and whether you allow delegated countersignature once Globex signs? Globex prefers to send the envelope from our side (DocuSign) and have Redwood sign as recipient, but our procurement team needs to know whether Redwood requires a specific title (e.g., VP Legal, CEO) or if an authorized delegate is acceptable.

Attachments noted: proposed redlines (we tracked a handful of operational clarifications and a subprocessor list question). Please confirm the signatory path and whether you require two-step authentication for external envelopes.

—Sarah
Sarah Turner
Sr. Contracts Manager, Globex Corporation

---
From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@globex.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + execution logistics

Sarah — thanks for the quick review and for the attachment. We received the PDF and have an internal view on signatory authority. High level: Redwood is fine receiving the envelope from Globex via DocuSign. We do allow delegated signatory for standard DPAs provided delegation is recorded and the signer's title/authority block is included in the signing tab. Our recommended path (to avoid delays):

1) Redwood signs first (Redwood VP Legal or delegate) in DocuSign as Recipient 1.
2) Globex signs after (Recipient 2).

If Globex prefers to send first that also works — we just ask for an explicit “Countersign allowed” checkbox or a short confirmation in the envelope comments so our Legal Ops team can match audit records. We will not require CEO-level execution for this customer; VP Legal or General Counsel sign-off is sufficient per our delegation matrix.

I've attached our redlines (Redwood_DPA_Globex_redlines_20271115.pdf) and a short signing instructions doc (Signing_Instructions_Redwood.docx). Neha, can you confirm the required authentication level (SMS vs. DocuSign ID) and whether we should require sign-in for the Redwood recipient?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Contracts Ops, Redwood Inference

---
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Redwood DPA redlines + execution logistics

Tessa / Neha —

Routing recommendation from Legal Ops (to minimize countersign friction):
- Prefer Redwood to sign first when we are the party making commercial concessions (so audit trail shows our acceptance). If Globex insists on sending first, that is ok; we still require a clear counter-signature placeholder for Redwood.
- Signer identity: VP Legal (Neha Kapoor) or her documented delegate are acceptable. Our stored delegation spreadsheet lists the acceptable delegates — make sure the delegate name is present in the envelope recipient field.
- Authentication: SMS OTP for the Redwood signer is sufficient for this counterparty. No additional ID verification required unless Globex requests higher assurance.
- Envelope settings: set recipient routing order (1 = Redwood, 2 = Globex), require signer title field, and include a non-editable comment: "Countersign allowed by Redwood Legal". Add CC to procurement@globex.com for their records.

Also flagged: Globex asked about subprocessors/data transfer language in clause 5. We should include our subprocessor list link in the envelope (link to Drive) rather than embedding the whole appendix to keep the DocuSign payload small. See attached Signing_Instructions_Redwood.docx for the exact link.

Laura Bennett
Head, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference

---
From: James Liu <james.liu@globex.com>
To: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@globex.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@globex.com
Date: Sat, 20 Nov 2027 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + execution logistics

Thanks, all — confirming Globex will prepare the DocuSign envelope and send to Redwood as Recipient 1 per the attached order. A couple of operational points so our teams don't get stuck:

- Envelope ID: 0f3a-GLX-2027-5744 (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/envelope/ABC123456789)
- We will place a required field for "Signer title" and a checkbox for "I confirm I have authority to sign on behalf of Globex."
- Globex procurement requests that Redwood include the same authority confirmation for its signer. Can Redwood include a short text field for the Redwood signer to confirm delegation (e.g., "I am authorized to sign per Redwood delegation spreadsheet")?
- We will CC procurement@globex.com. If Redwood would prefer to countersign after we initiate, please confirm whether we should leave Redwood as Recipient 2 instead.

For now we will send the envelope with Redwood as Recipient 1 because it sounds like Redwood prefers to sign first. Once we send it I'll follow up with a status ping.

—James
Contracts & Procurement, Globex
